story.iWant: robust error handling throughout the weather intelligence layer
story.soThat: all failure scenarios are handled gracefully with appropriate user-facing messages
story.tasks:
Task 1: Create error handler module with error mapping (AC: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5) - Create /lib/error-handler.ts module - Define ErrorCode type: 'timeout' | 'invalid_location' | 'service_unavailable' | 'network_error' | 'unknown_error' - Define ApiError interface: { code: ErrorCode, message: string, statusCode: number } - Implement mapErrorToApiError(error: unknown): ApiError function - Map timeout errors (AbortError) to 'timeout' code with 504 status - Map 404 errors to 'invalid_location' code with 404 status - Map 5xx errors to 'service_unavailable' code with 500 status - Map network errors (TypeError: Failed to fetch) to 'network_error' code with 503 status - Map unknown errors to 'unknown_error' code with 500 status - Add user-friendly messages for each error type
Task 2: Implement server-side error logging (AC: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5) - Create logError(error: unknown, context: string): void function in error-handler.ts - Log full error details including stack trace to console.error - Include context parameter (e.g., "OpenWeather API", "API Route") - Log timestamp and error type for debugging - Never expose stack traces or internal paths to users - Ensure logs are visible in Vercel serverless function logs
Task 3: Implement API error response helper (AC: 5) - Create createErrorResponse(apiError: ApiError): NextResponse function - Return NextResponse.json with format: { error: { code, message } } - Set appropriate HTTP status code from apiError.statusCode - Add 'Content-Type: application/json' header - Ensure consistent response format across all error types
Task 4: Add retry logic for OpenWeather API (AC: 1) - Update /lib/openweather.ts to add retry capability - Wrap fetchForecast() with retry logic for 5xx errors - Implement single retry attempt (max 1 retry) - Use exponential backoff: 1 second delay before retry - Log retry attempts server-side - If retry fails, throw error for upstream handling - Do NOT retry on 404, timeout, or network errors (only 5xx)
Task 5: Integrate error handler into API route (AC: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5) - Import error handler functions into /app/api/check-rain/route.ts - Wrap main route logic in try/catch block - Catch all errors and pass to mapErrorToApiError() - Log errors with context using logError(error, 'API Route') - Return error response using createErrorResponse() - Ensure analytics logging doesn't interfere with error handling (fire-and-forget) - Test error handling doesn't break existing success paths
Task 6: Create TypeScript type definitions (AC: 5) - Create /types/error.ts file (or add to existing types file) - Export ErrorCode type with all error code literals - Export ApiError interface - Export ErrorResponse interface for API response format - Add JSDoc comments for all types
Task 7: Update environment variable documentation (AC: 1, 2, 3, 4) - Add error handling notes to README or .env.example - Document retry behavior for 5xx errors - Document timeout threshold (5 seconds) - Document error response format - Note that analytics failures don't trigger error responses (fire-and-forget)
Task 8: Manual testing and validation (AC: 1-5) - Test 404 error: Invalid location → Verify 404, invalid_location code - Test 5xx error: Simulate OpenWeather downtime → Verify retry attempt, then service_unavailable - Test timeout: Simulate >5s delay → Verify 504, timeout code, request aborted - Test network error: Disconnect internet → Verify network_error code - Test success path still works: Valid location → Verify 200 response unchanged - Verify error response format: All errors return { error: { code, message } } - Verify server logs: Stack traces visible in console, not in response - TypeScript compilation passes (npm run type-check) - ESLint validation passes (npm run lint)

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: AC1: OpenWeather API 5xx errors trigger single retry attempt, with full error logging AC2: Timeout errors (>5 seconds) return timeout error code with 504 status, AbortController cancels request AC3: Invalid location errors (404) return invalid_location code with 404 status, friendly message AC4: Network errors distinguished from API errors, return network_error code AC5: Consistent error response format for all error types, with HTTP status codes matching error types, no technical details exposed to users

doc.title: Epic 2 Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Error handler module creates /lib/error-handler.ts with mapErrorToResponse() for standardized error codes. Timeout errors (AbortError) map to timeout code. 404 errors map to invalid_location. 5xx errors map to service_unavailable. Network errors map to network_error. All errors logged server-side with stack traces, user-facing errors contain friendly messages only.

doc.title: Epics Document
doc.snippet: As a developer, I want robust error handling throughout the weather intelligence layer, so that all failure scenarios are handled gracefully. OpenWeather API failures (5xx errors) trigger single retry attempt. Timeout errors (>5 seconds) return timeout error response. Invalid location errors return specific error code with suggestions. Network errors are distinguished from API errors. All error responses follow consistent format. Technical error details are logged but not exposed to users.

doc.title: Previous Story 2.7
doc.snippet: API route structure: POST handler implements complete decision logic flow with 8 STEP comments. Analytics call positioned at STEP 2 (after validation, before weather fetch) using fire-and-forget pattern. Code quality standards: Comprehensive JSDoc comments, TypeScript strict mode with no any types, clear error handling with try/catch blocks. Module integration pattern: Import functions from lib/ modules at top of route.ts, handle errors appropriately.

file.reason: Main API endpoint that needs comprehensive error handling. Currently has basic try/catch with OpenWeatherError handling (lines 207-233). Needs to be enhanced with centralized error handler integration.
HTTP client with timeout and retry logic. Currently implements single retry for 5xx errors (lines 68-73). This is the retry logic that Story 2.8 builds upon. Throws OpenWeatherError with error codes.

story-context.constraints: - Centralized error mapping in /lib/error-handler.ts for consistent error handling across all failure scenarios - Server-side logging with full stack traces, user-facing messages without technical details or internal paths - Error codes enable frontend to show appropriate UI messages (e.g., different messaging for timeout vs invalid location) - Graceful degradation: All errors return proper HTTP status codes (404, 500, 503, 504) and JSON responses - Single retry attempt for 5xx errors only (API server errors), 1 second exponential backoff before retry - Do NOT retry on 404 (invalid location), timeout, or network errors - 5 second timeout threshold already implemented in Story 2.1 via AbortController - Timeout errors mapped to timeout error code with 504 status, AbortController cancels pending request - Consistent JSON structure: { error: { code: ErrorCode, message: string } } for all error types - Analytics logging (fire-and-forget) must not interfere with error handling - Error handling must preserve existing success paths (don't break working features) - Error logs visible in Vercel serverless function logs for production debugging - TypeScript strict mode with no any types, comprehensive JSDoc comments on all exported functions

interface.name: ErrorResponse
interface.signature: interface ErrorResponse { error: ErrorCode; message: string; }

interface.name: OpenWeatherError
interface.signature: class OpenWeatherError extends Error { constructor(code: ErrorCode, message: string, statusCode?: number); }

tests.standards: Epic 2 uses manual testing approach via curl or Postman. No automated unit tests (deferred to Epic 5 per tech spec). TypeScript compilation validation (npm run type-check) and ESLint validation (npm run lint) required. Server-side log verification in terminal or Vercel logs for debugging.
